newsitem.title: POLAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Celuloza long-term buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Celuloza long-term buy.

text.p: Shares of Poland's largest paper firm Celuloza SA are worth buying only in the longer term, as the firm's current valuation seemed demanding given its planned expenditure and increasing competition, Nomura said.

A Nomura Equity Research report dated April 23 said Celuloza's planned 800 million zlotys in investment and its potential majority shareholder in Austrian firm Frantschach were good signs only in the longer term.

"The opening price of 20.5 zlotys is demanding given that the company's planned expenditure will depress future earnings and that competition in Poland is growing. The shares are worth buying, but only on a longer-term view," the report said.
Celuloza on April 25 started trade 4.9 percent above its issue price of 20.5 zlotys and closed on Monday at 20.7 zlotys.

A consortium led by Mondi, a unit of Anglo-American Corp of South Africa, and its Austrian subsidiary Frantschach AG, is currently the sole bidder in the treasury ministry's offer of 65 percent of Celuloza shares.

Nomura said a good sign was that demand for paper and board products was growing strongly in Poland but so was competition, particularly in corrugated board, where a number of Western European firms had built greenfields or made acquisitions.
Celuloza made a net profit of 73 million zlotys last year and only five million zlotys in this year's first quarter despite its 73-million-zloty 1997 net forecast.

In its report written before the above information was published, Nomura predicted Celuloza would make a net profit of 88.3 million zlotys last year, 75.2 million this year and 108.7 million next year.
Return on equity would be at 20.9 percent, 15.6 percent and 21.5 percent in those three years, the report said.
